**My thinking:**

I've been farming this land since I was a young woman, and my mother farmed it before me. Everyone in our village grows the same things — winter wheat, then summer maize on the same fields. That's what this land is for. I don't need to think too hard about this. The soil here on the plain is good for grain. We have the well for irrigation.

My husband went to work in Tianjin three years ago, so I manage the fields myself, about 8 mu total. I can't handle anything too complicated or that needs a lot of new learning. My neighbor Old Zhang and I watch each other's fields and share the rotary tiller.

For wheat, I'll plant in October, same as always. I buy the seeds from the village supply station — they sell the good Jimai variety everyone uses. I'll do the base fertilizer before planting, then put urea on in spring when the shoots are coming up. I irrigate before winter sets in, again at jointing, and once more when the heads fill out. Three waterings, same as every year.

After wheat harvest in June, I'll plant maize right away. I use Zhengdan 958, the hybrid — everyone switched to this years ago because the yield is better. If summer rains are good I may only need one irrigation. I spray for pests twice, once early and once if I see problems.

I keep a small patch near the house for vegetables — garlic, beans — but that's just for eating, not for the plan here.
